title: Tidal Cycles – Live Coding Music with Algorithmic Patterns
summary: Tidal Cycles (or 'Tidal') is a free and open-source live coding environment for creating algorithmic music patterns. Written in Haskell, it leverages SuperCollider for sound synthesis and MIDI. Tidal enables users to generate complex sequences, including polyphonic and polyrhythmic patterns, through code. It has inspired similar open-source projects like Strudel and fosters a vibrant community of musicians and developers focused on algorithmic music composition and improvisation.
key_points: Tidal Cycles is a free/open-source live coding environment for algorithmic music patterns.
Written in Haskell and uses SuperCollider for synthesis and MIDI.
Allows creation of flexible sequences (polyphonic, polyrhythmic, generative).
Inspired a family of similar open-source tools, including web-based Strudel.
Supported by a diverse community for composition, improvisation, and exploration of algorithmic music.
